content.value_statement: Mass spectrometry workflows require careful file handling, signal processing, and identification steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical PyOpenMS analysis patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to load, inspect, and write mzML, mzXML, mzTab, FASTA, idXML, and featureXML data.
Guides spectral smoothing, filtering, centroiding, normalization, and peak picking with PyOpenMS algorithms.
Shows feature detection, feature linking, consensus map handling, and table export for quantitative analysis.
Supports peptide and protein identification workflows, including FDR filtering and score interpretation.
Covers metabolomics preprocessing, blank filtering, missing value imputation, and compound mass matching.
limitations: Does not provide raw experimental data or validate scientific conclusions.
Requires PyOpenMS and related search engines to be installed separately.
Examples may need adaptation for local paths, instrument settings, and study design.
Does not replace expert review of proteomics or metabolomics methods.

use_cases.title: Build LC-MS/MS Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan file loading, signal processing, feature detection, and quantitative export steps for a proteomics project.

use_cases.title: Integrate PyOpenMS Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use established PyOpenMS objects and file formats when adding mass spectrometry support to data tools.

use_cases.title: Review Identification Results
use_cases.description: Inspect peptide and protein IDs, apply FDR filtering, and summarize score context for reports.

prompt_templates.title: Load a Mass Spectrometry File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pyopenms skill to show how to load sample.mzML, count spectra, and inspect the first spectrum.

prompt_templates.title: Process and Detect Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pyopenms to outline a workflow for smoothing, centroiding, and detecting features from LC-MS data.

prompt_templates.title: Review Peptide Identifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pyopenms to guide FDR filtering and q-value interpretation for an idXML peptide identification file.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Metabolomics Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use pyopenms to design an untargeted metabolomics workflow from mzML files to an analysis-ready feature table.

output_examples.output: A workflow describing file loading, spectrum counts, retention time checks, and peak inspection steps.
A checklist for loading idXML data, applying FDR filtering, reviewing q-values, and summarizing peptide and protein hits.
A workflow covering feature detection, alignment, consensus mapping, blank filtering, missing value handling, and table export.

best_practices: Start with read-only exploration before writing converted files or feature tables.
Record search parameters, enzyme settings, tolerances, and FDR thresholds with every result.
Keep raw data, intermediate files, and exported tables separated by project stage.
anti_patterns: Do not run examples on irreplaceable files without copies or versioned outputs.
Do not compare samples before checking retention time alignment and feature linking quality.
Do not report peptide or metabolite matches without score, tolerance, and FDR context.

faq.question: What is PyOpenMS used for?
faq.answer: PyOpenMS provides Python bindings for OpenMS mass spectrometry workflows in proteomics and metabolomics.

faq.question: Does this skill install PyOpenMS automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but users must manage installation in their own environment.

faq.question: Which file formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common formats such as mzML, mzXML, mzTab, FASTA, idXML, featureXML, and consensusXML.

faq.question: Can it help with peptide identification?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains loading identification data, applying FDR filtering, and interpreting peptide and protein scores.

faq.question: Can it support metabolomics analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers feature detection, consensus mapping, blank filtering, imputation, and mass-based compound matching.

faq.question: Does it replace scientific validation?
faq.answer: No. Results still require expert review, study-specific controls, and appropriate statistical validation.
